title: Practice Log
description: One practice rep and its outcome. Two doctrine rules are structural here. First, the process is scored and the outcome is not: `outcome` is a closed vocabulary describing what happened, and there is deliberately NO field for a phone number, a contact detail, a match or any other trophy, because what gets logged is what gets optimized. Second, a rep involves a real person who did not agree to be in a file, so this record holds no person reference at all: a third party can only appear in an interaction_debrief, and there only as a given name.

date.description: Practice date, logged on the day rather than on Sunday from memory

tier.description: Floor survives a bad day and needs no other person. Deep is never the minimum and never the measure of self-respect.

context.description: A generic category. There is no free-text venue field.

ladder_rung.description: The approach anxiety ladder rung, where the rep came from one

completed.description: Whether the rep ran to its designed end. A session ended on a stop rule is completed, not failed.

prediction.description: What the user predicted would happen, written BEFORE the rep, so calibration can be measured

outcome.description: A closed vocabulary. `no_received_and_respected` is a clean outcome, not a failure: a run that ends in a no and a clean exit is a successful run.

discomfort_peak.description: The peak matters more than the endpoint for judging habituation and for triggering a stop rule

process_score.description: The only score. All seven true is a clean run, including when the answer was no.

lesson.description: One local lesson about this rep. Never a global belief about the self, which is the wrong lesson this log exists to prevent.

allOf.description: A completed rep records what happened and how it felt, so habituation can be judged across sessions.
A rep stopped on a stop rule must name which rule fired.
